method: Both the retiring SwissJob scraper and the new Core adapter were replayed offline against this SAME sealed capture, so the parity below is byte-level and not two independent samples.

transport_contract.detail_url: the listing card's own href, absolute

pagination_finding.note: `?p=` barely paginates: page 3 repeats page 2 exactly and pages 3-4 add nothing. The scraper's cursor early-stop fires on the first fully-known page, so on a cold run it stops at page 3 and NEVER sees the four offers that only appear on page 5. Core sweeps the declared five pages instead of early-stopping, so those four are harvested; the request cost is bounded by the same five pages.

deliberate_improvements.what: published_at now carries the portal's own date
deliberate_improvements.evidence: 97 of 97 listing records expose <time datetime>; the detail page repeats it as schema.org datePosted. All 115 production rows have no date because the scraper never read it.
deliberate_improvements.effect: Core resolves currency and recency from the portal's date instead of having none. A record without a usable ISO date omits the field entirely, so absent still means UNKNOWN.

deliberate_improvements.what: identity is the portal's numeric id, not the URL
deliberate_improvements.evidence: 26 of 26 URLs match /jobs/id<digits>-<slug>, and the slug carries the job title.
deliberate_improvements.effect: A retitled offer keeps one identity. The scraper keyed on the URL, so a retitle produced a second offer.

deliberate_improvements.what: the declared five pages are always swept
deliberate_improvements.evidence: the pagination finding above: four offers of 26 live only on page 5, behind a fully-known page 3.
deliberate_improvements.effect: Those offers enter the corpus. Cost stays at five listing pages per run.

reported_not_changed.what: the detail page's Arbeitsort / Funktion / Pensum metadata
reported_not_changed.evidence: .descriptor labels exist (Arbeitsort 26, Funktion 26, Pensum 8 of 26) but never inside the same .long_value_row as a .long_value, so the scraper's loop skips every row — which is why employment_type is empty for all 115 production rows.
reported_not_changed.why_not_changed: Reading them would change what the corpus contains for every offer, and Funktion is not an employment type. It is a finding, not a migration step.

traffic.core_per_run: 5 listing pages + 26 detail pages = 31 requests, paced at the portal's own 2 s
traffic.note: Core has no description cursor on purpose: the descriptions run to 9.866 characters and truncating them to fit a scope cursor would alter five of 26 offers on every cycle.

notes: No credential exists for this source and none was created; the sweep is anonymous HTTPS.
The artifact carries no personal data: only byte counts, hashes and aggregate counters.
The scraper module and its tests stay in SwissJob as the branch rollback path; only its registry entry is gone.
